subject: physics
title: Radioactive Decay and Half-Life
welcome_lead: Watch unstable nuclei tick away exponentially with N = N₀ e^(−λt).
meta_desc: A-Level Nuclear adventure on decay law, decay constant and half-life.
final_note: Half-life and decay constant are linked by t½ = ln 2 / λ.

concepts.def: Decays per second, A = λN, measured in Bq.
λ = probability of decay per second.
Time for activity to halve: t½ = ln 2 / λ.
Each nucleus decays unpredictably and independently.

walkthroughs.body_html: Number of undecayed nuclei drops exponentially. Equally, activity A = A₀ e^(−λt). λ is the decay constant in s⁻¹.
Half-life t½ is the time for N (or A) to drop to half its initial value. After n half-lives, N = N₀ / 2ⁿ. Formula: t½ = ln 2 / λ ≈ 0.693 / λ.
Each individual decay is random and spontaneous, but with huge numbers of atoms the average follows the exponential law very closely.
